newsitem.title: UK: Euro HS fuel sold lower, LS cargo held up by paper.
newsitem.headline: Euro HS fuel sold lower, LS cargo held up by paper.

text.p: European high sulphur barge prices were pressured downwards by aggressive selling on Wednesday while low sulphur markets were supported by strong swaps levels, traders said.
First deals in the barge market were struck at $83.25 and $83.50 fob a tonne in Antwerp. But later trades were done at $81.50 to finish the day $2 lower than yesterday.
"The prompt was getting knocked down very aggressively," said one trader, who said bunker demand had been very weak for the whole day.
Some distressed Russian cracked cargoes weighed on the Rotterdam market and two were believed picked up in the low $80's, traders said.
Low sulphur swaps were firm at $96.50/$97.25 for June, with New York harbour prices still seen as supportive.
But physical business was quiet, with Friday's deal seen as having stymied the market.

"Near-term barrels are not being shown. It has all gone quiet since the last deal, which rather surprised the market," one trader said. "Physical is definetly under June swaps at the moment but its unclear by how much."
Prompt one percent supplies were tight, traders said.
